chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Lucky Millinder, bandleaders who sing and dance, and Ellington at seventy
summary: Collins compares Millinder and Calloway's showmanship with Duke, who only danced and sang at seventy.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Tyree, yeah. Oh, he just had everybody, you know, yeah. So it was a great band. And at this time Millinder also there was another singer, entertainer, Lucky Milner was -- now, he had the -- what was it, the -- what did he call his band? Blue Rhythm Ribbon. Yeah, Lucky Millinder's Blue Rhythm Ribbon something, you know. But he was -- he was almost equally as popular in the same format as Cab Calloway, and Lucky kept -- had a very good band also.

Really, I think that Dizzy was in his band at one time, and I can't recall who was in the band, but I know during this same time this was a fad then, you know. The hidey ho and the singing and the dancing of the leaders, you know. So of course Duke was always Duke. He didn't sing nor dance, at that time. He danced in later years, when he got 70.
He sang a little, you know. He -- Tell it like it T-I-Z,
Yeah, he had to wait until he was 70, you know.
